answer: A stake-and-slash bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and misbehavior burns part of it. Like a tundra crossing at dawn, the crossing is slow and cold for a crowd of clones — each new identity pays the same toll, so a Sybil farm cost scales linearly while honest agents earn the bond back. A velvet rope is not enough; only a real economic cost stops cheap clones.
